akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ﴾: its singular is "العِهْنَة", like "الصُوف" and "الصُّوفَة" (wool, a tuft of wool). As for His words ﴿مَا هِيَهْ﴾ with the hāʾ, it is because the pause on it is made with the hāʾ, since it is the end of a verse.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الْقَارِعَةُ﴾, that is, the Resurrection, which strikes the hearts with its terrors.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا الْقَارِعَةُ﴾: a magnifying of the dread of its matter. They are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), [together] the khabar of «القارعة».

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾ — made you know — ﴿مَا الْقَارِعَةُ﴾: a further magnifying of its dread. The first «ما» is a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is its khabar; and the second «ما» with its khabar is in the position of the second object of «أدرى».

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: what makes it accusative is indicated by «القارعة», that is, «تقرع» ("it strikes"), ﴿يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ﴾: like a swarm of scattered locusts, surging into one another in bewilderment until they are summoned to the reckoning,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ﴾: like carded wool in the lightness of their movement, until they are level with the earth.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾, in that his good deeds outweigh his bad deeds,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾ in the Garden, that is, one of contentment, in that he is content with it, that is, pleasing to him.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾, in that his bad deeds outweigh his good deeds,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ﴾, that is, what Hāwiya is.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ﴾: intensely hot. The hāʾ of «هيه» is the hāʾ of pause (li-l-sakt); it is retained in continuous reading and in pausing, and in one reading it is dropped in continuous reading.

daas-irab:10-10.t: Like the i'rab of verse 3, and the hāʾ is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿نارٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حامِيَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is explicative (mufassira).

daas-irab:5-5.t: Conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle (ḥarf istiʾnāf); ﴿أما﴾ is a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), because the relative noun resembles the conditional; ﴿هو﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿راضِيَةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ مَن.

daas-irab:8-8.t: Conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ مَن.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿الْقارِعَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مَا الْقارِعَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of القارعة, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَا الْقارِعَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَكُونُ النَّاسُ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun; ﴿كَالْفَراشِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of يكون; ﴿الْمَبْثُوثِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الفراش; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

dervis-irab:1-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقارِعَةُ): the Resurrection, which strikes (taqraʿu) the hearts with its terrors. In al-Mukhtār: «Qaraʿa is of the pattern of qaṭaʿa, and al-qāriʿa is a severe one among the hardships of time, namely the calamity (al-dāhiya).» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Qaraʿtu al-bāb qarʿan means: I knocked at the door and tapped on it.»
(الفراش): In al-Qāmūs: «Al-farāsha is that which throws itself into the lamp; the plural is farāsh. Of a lock, it is the part that catches in it; also any thin bone, a little water, a light (frivolous) man, a village between Baghdad and al-Ḥilla, a place in the desert, and a proper name; and Darb Farāsha is a quarter of Baghdad. Al-farāsh, on the pattern of saḥāb, is the mud that dries on the ground after the water [is gone]; of nabīdh, it is the bubbles that remain on it; it is also two green veins under the tongue, and the two pieces of iron by which the cheek-straps are tied to the bridle. With kasra (al-firāsh) it is what is spread out, the plural being furush; also a man's wife — and it is said that «وفرش مرفوعة» is from this — a bird's nest, and the place of the tongue at the bottom of the mouth.» The author of al-Munjid confused matters, merging al-farāsha and al-firāsh into a single entry and making «the light man» one of the meanings of al-firāsh, whereas it is in fact farāsha. More on the meaning of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric.
(الْمَبْثُوثِ): scattered and spread out. One says: so-and-so spread his bounty (basaṭa khayrahu), dispersed it (baththahu) and distributed it (baqqahu), when he made it ample. [The poet] said:
وبسط الخير لنا وبقّه ... فالناس طرا يأكلون رزقه
(He spread out bounty for us and dispersed it, so all people eat of his provision.)
(العهن): red wool; its singular is ʿihna.
(الْمَنْفُوشِ): a passive participle from al-nafsh, which — as in al-Qāmūs — is pulling a thing apart with your fingers until it spreads out, like al-tanfīsh; and al-nafash, with the middle letter vowelled, is wool. Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «One says: nafashtu the wool and the cotton and sabbakhtuhu, when you have teased it out and lightened it, as the carder does. Pieces of cotton and what falls off during carding are called al-sabīkha, plural sabāʾikh. And one says: sabbakha Allāhu ʿanka al-ḥummā, i.e. may Allah lighten the fever for you and draw it out of you. From this is [the report] that the Prophet ﷺ saw ʿĀʾisha invoking [Allah] against a thief who had robbed her, and he said: Do not lighten [his sin] for him (lā tusabbikhī ʿanhu) by your invoking against him.»

* I'rab:
(الْقارِعَةُ مَا الْقارِعَةُ): its i'rab has preceded at «الحاقة ما الحاقة». (وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ): its i'rab has preceded at «ما أدراك ما الحاقة», so refresh your memory of it there.
(يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَراشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ): the ẓarf (adverb of time) is accusative by an implied [verb] indicated by «القارعة», i.e. it strikes the hearts with its terrors on the Day of Resurrection. It is not permissible for it to be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the first «القارعة», because of the separation between them by the khabar (predicate), nor to the second or the third, because the adverb does not fit with them in meaning. The clause «يكون» is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; «الناس» is the noun (ism) of «يكون», «كالفراش» is its predicate, and «المبثوث» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الفراش». It is also permissible that «يكون» be complete (tāmma), so that «الناس» is a fāʿil (agent) and «كالفراش» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of the complete «يكون», i.e. they come into being and are gathered in the state of being like moths.
(وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ): conjoined to the previous verse, matching it in its i'rab.
(فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ): the fāʾ is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya); «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing; «من» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «ثقلت موازينه» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من», with no grammatical position; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa) because of the sense of condition in the relative; «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ and «في عيشة» is its khabar; «راضية» is an adjective; and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first, which is «من». The meaning of «راضية» will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ): conjoined to the previous sentence; «أمه» is a mubtadaʾ and «هاوية» is the khabar of «أمه», and the clause is the khabar of «من».
(وَما أَدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause «أدراك» is the khabar; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and «هي» is the khabar; the hāʾ is for pausing (hāʾ al-sakt); and the clause «ما هيه», suspended [from the verb] by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of «أدراك». Al-Hāwiya is one of the names of Hell; it is the abyss whose bottom is not reached and whose depth is not plumbed. Qatāda said: it is an Arabic expression; when a man fell into a severe affair, it was said: «هوت أمه» (his mother has fallen). It is also said that what is meant is the «mother of his head» (umm raʾsihi), i.e. they fall into the Fire on their heads. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «"فأمه هاوية" is from their saying, when they invoke destruction upon a man, "hawat ummuhu" (his mother has fallen), because when he falls (hawā), i.e. drops and perishes, his mother has fallen in bereavement and grief. [The poet] said:
هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح غاديا ... وماذا يردّ الليل حين يئوب
(May his mother perish! What does the morning send forth when he sets out early, and what does the night bring back when he returns!)»
The verse is by Kaʿb, in an elegy for his brother. «هوت أمه» is an invocation by which actual occurrence is not intended, but rather wonder. «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and what follows it is the khabar; the meaning is: what thing does the morning send forth of him, and what thing does the night bring back? One must assume an abstractive (tajrīdiyya) «منه» — meaning that he would set out in the morning in pursuit of raiding and return at night victorious. «ما» in both places is interrogative in form, its meaning being wonder and magnification; and attributing the verb to the morning and the night is figurative (majāz).
(نارٌ حامِيَةٌ): «نار» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هي», and «حامية» is an adjective. Omission of the mubtadaʾ is frequent in the answer to a question, after the fāʾ of the answer, and after [the verb of] saying.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «القارعة ما القارعة وما أدراك ما القارعة» there is the device of repetition (al-takrīr), the purpose being to make its matter terrifying and to magnify its horror. Its discussion has preceded many times.
2- In His saying «يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش» there are two splendid similes; each is a mursal mujmal simile (with the particle of comparison stated and the point of similarity omitted), because the point of similarity has been omitted. In the first, the points of similarity are many, among them:
1- the giddiness that has overtaken them; 2- their spreading out over the earth; 3- their climbing on top of one another; 4- the multitude that is of no avail; 5- weakness, abasement and answering the caller from every direction; 6- flying into the fire to be burned without wanting to be burned.
As for the comparison of the mountains to carded wool, it too is a mursal mujmal simile, and the points of similarity are also many, among them:
1- their crumbling and collapse; 2- their becoming like wool; 3- then their becoming like scattered dust. The poets clung to these meanings. Jarīr said, satirising al-Farazdaq:
أبلغ بني وقبان أن حلومهم ... خفّت فما يزنون حبة خردل
أزرى بحلمكم الفياش فأنتم ... مثل الفراش غشين نار المصطلي
(Tell the Banū Waqbān that their minds have grown light, so they do not weigh a mustard seed; boasting has disgraced your forbearance, so you are like moths that swarm into the fire of one warming himself.)
And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī said in an elegy for his father:
فيا ليت شعري هل يخف وقاره ... إذا صار أحد في القيامة كالعهن
وهل يرد الحوض الرويّ مبادرا ... مع الناس أم يأبى الزحام فيستأني
(Would that I knew: will his dignity grow light when [Mount] Uḥud becomes like wool at the Resurrection? And will he hasten to the thirst-quenching Basin with the people, or will he shun the crowding and wait patiently?)
[The poem] begins:
نقمت الرضا حتى على ضاحك المزن ... فلا جادني إلا عبوس من الدّجن
وليت فمي إن شاء سنى تبسمي ... فم الطعنة النجلاء تدمى بلا سن
(I have come to resent contentment, even in the laughing [lightning-lit] rain-cloud, so let nothing water me but a frowning, overcast sky; and would that my mouth, if it wished the gleam of my smile, were the mouth of a wide spear-wound that bleeds without a tooth.)
3- In His saying «فهو في عيشة راضية» there is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope), since the one who is pleased with it is the one who lives in it; so it is a majāz mursal whose relation is that of place (al-maḥalliyya). It is also said that «راضية» means «مرضية» (pleasing). The first to write on the figures (majāzāt) of the Qur'an, at the end of the second century AH, was Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā in his book «Majāz al-Qur'an», to which we have referred in this book. He prefaces his book with an introduction on general linguistic studies of the Qur'an, beginning it with a study of the word «Qur'an». He has a particular view on the derivation of this word that later scholars transmit from him, namely his saying: «It was called Qur'an only because it gathers the sūras and joins them together; and the explanation of that is a verse in the Qur'an: Allah, exalted be His praise, said: إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه.» He adduces evidence for it from the speech of the Arabs, and after that proceeds to the text of the Qur'an and the modes of speech it contains, pointing out that the Qur'an resembles the speech of the Arabs in its composition. He says: «In the Qur'an there is the like of what is in the speech of the Arabs of the aspects of i'rab and meanings.» He mentions those aspects with examples and treats them in detail. Regarding this verse he said: «Among the figures is where the object falls to the agent. He said: "كالذي ينعق بما لا يسمع" — the meaning is upon the sheep that is shouted at, and it was shifted to the shepherd who shouts at the sheep. And He said: "كالنهار مبصرا"; it has two figures, one of them being that the Arabs placed things of their speech in the position of the agent while the meaning is that it is an object, because it is a vessel (ẓarf) in which something else acts, and because the day does not see; rather the one who looks sees in it. And in the Qur'an: "في عيشة راضية", whereas only the one who lives in it is pleased with it.» The upshot regarding the book al-Majāz is that it was a step on the way to discussing the modes of expression, or majāz in its general sense. He attempted to uncover some of what came of that in the style of the Qur'an, comparing it with what came in Arabic literature, aided by his abundant learning in it.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ﴾.
He means: like a swarm of locusts climbing over one another; likewise people on that Day will surge into one another.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "كالصوف المنفوش" (like carded wool). It has been mentioned that the forms of the mountains are moved across the earth while, in the shape of mountains, they are like fine dust.
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ﴾.
Because their colours differ, like the colours of dyed wool (العهن).

farraa:6-6.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾.
[That is,] and his weight (وزنه). The Arabs say: هل لك فى درهم بميزان درهمك ووزن درهمك (Would you like a dirham of the weight of your dirham?), and they say: دارى بميزان دارك ووزن دارك (my house is the equal [lit. the balance/weight] of your house). The poet said:
قد كنتُ قبلَ لقائِكم ذا مِرَّةٍ * عندى لكلٍ مخاصم ميزانه
(Before meeting you I was a man of strength: I had, for every disputant, his match [lit. his balance].)
He means: I had [what matched] the weight of his speech and [could] refute it.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ﴾.
It has become his abode, as a woman gives shelter to her son; so, since he has no abode other than it, He made it a mother to him.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «القارعة»: khabar (predicate); and the clause is the khabar of the preceding mubtadaʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The wāw is resumptive; the clause «ما القارعة» is the second object of «أدراك»; and the clause «وما أدراك» is conjoined to the clause {مَا الْقَارِعَةُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «يوم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, its implied form being: تأتي يوم يكون (it comes on the day when …); and the clause (تأتي) is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «أمَّا»: a particle of condition and detailing; «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The fāʾ is the linking one, and the clause «هو في عيشة» is the khabar (predicate) of the preceding mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «وأمَّا مَنْ خَفَّت» is conjoined to the clause «أمَّا مَنْ ثقلت».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: (فأمه هاوية) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ (subject) {مَنْ خَفَّتْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «وما أدراك» is conjoined to the clause {فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ}, and the clause «ما هي» is the second object of «أدراك».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «نار»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: it is a blazing fire.

mekki-muskil:1-3.t: His saying, Exalted is He (القارعة ما القارعة وما أدراك ما القارعة): the discussion of it, and of what is like it — such as (وما أدراك ما هيه) and the like — has already preceded in al-Ḥāqqa, al-Wāqiʿa and al-Qadr, which makes repeating it unnecessary.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying (يوم يكون الناس): the governing word (ʿāmil) in (يوم) is (القارعة), i.e. it strikes the ears of creation on the day that ... And it was said: (القارعة) is nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied verb, and that verb is the governing word in (يوم), its implied form being «ستأتي القارعة» (the Striking Calamity will come). The first is better.
His saying (كالفراش): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna; and (كالعهن) is like it. (العهن) is the plural of «عهنة».

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (من ثقلت موازينه): (من) is conditional, a complete noun (ism tāmm), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (فهو) is the khabar (predicate). (من خفت) is like it.
His saying (هيه): the hāʾ entered for the pause (waqf), to make clear the vowel of the yāʾ.
His saying (نار): nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هي نار».

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as a second mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿القارعة﴾: khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause ﴿ما القارعة﴾, made of the second mubtadaʾ and its khabar, is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ ﴿القارعة﴾, and the clause ﴿القارعة ما القارعة﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or parenthetical, and «ما» is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو), referring back to ﴿ما﴾; the kāf is the pronoun of the addressee, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿القارعة﴾: khabar of the second ﴿ما﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the nominal clause ﴿ما القارعة﴾ is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of ﴿أدراك﴾, and the clause ﴿وما أدراك ...﴾ is conjoined to the preceding clause, or parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, its implied form being: "it will come" (تأتي), or "it will strike, on the day when..." (تقرع يوم يكون...إلخ).
﴿يكون﴾: a deficient imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الناس﴾: the noun (ism) of «يكون», nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿كالفراش﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «يكون», and «الفراش» is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿المبثوث﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of «الفراش», genitive (majrūr) by the kasra. Or ﴿يكون﴾ is complete (tāmma) and «الناس» is the fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of the complete «يكون»; the clause ﴿يكون الناس﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it, and the clause ﴿يوم يكون...﴾, on the implied reading "it will come" (تأتي) or "it will strike on the day when..." (تقرع يوم يكون), is a resumption by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وتكون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿تكون﴾ is a deficient imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الجبال﴾: the noun (ism) of «تكون», nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿كالعهن﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «تكون», and ﴿العهن﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿المنفوش﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of «العهن», genitive (majrūr) by the kasra. Or ﴿تكون﴾ is a complete (tāmm) verb and «الجبال» is the fāʿil (agent), and in ﴿كالعهن﴾ the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of the complete ﴿تكون﴾; the clause ﴿تكون الجبال...﴾ is in the position of genitive, conjoined to ﴿يكون الناس﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿فأما﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, for drawing a consequence (tafrīʿiyya), and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿ثقلت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is a particle of the feminine.
﴿موازينه﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿ثقلت موازينه﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فهو﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa) because of the conditional sense in the relative noun, and ﴿هو﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as a second mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿في عيشة﴾: «في» is a preposition, and «عيشة» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by «في», the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿فهو في عيشة﴾, made of the second mubtadaʾ and its khabar, is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ ﴿من﴾.
﴿راضية﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of «عيشة», genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿خفت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is a particle of the feminine.
﴿موازينه﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿خفت موازينه﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿أما من خفت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أما من ثقلت﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿فأمه﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «أمه» is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿هاوية﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative by the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is parenthetical or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). «ما» is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو), referring back to ﴿ما﴾; the kāf is the pronoun of the addressee, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿هيه﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as khabar, and the hāʾ is for pausing (al-sakt); the clause ﴿ما هيه﴾ is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of ﴿أدرى﴾, and the clause ﴿وما أدراك ما هيه﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿هاوية﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿نار﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "it" (هي).
﴿حامية﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نار﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause is a resumption by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
It is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is in the clause; and it has been said: it is nominative on the implication of a verb, the implied form being:
"The Calamity (al-qāriʿa) will come". Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: الْقارِعَةُ is one of the names of the Resurrection, which Allah magnified and warned of.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: The hāʾ was brought because among the Arabs are those who say هي with the yāʾ quiescent, so the hāʾ is kept in the dialect of those who vowel it, to distinguish between it and the dialect of those who make it quiescent. If you join (the word to what follows), it is not permissible to keep the hāʾ, because the vowel has then been established. The correct course is to pause on it, following the codex (al-sawād), and not commit a grammatical error. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: whoever says "I join it, intending the pause" is mistaken, because it would follow for him that he should not inflect nouns in connected speech while intending the pause. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear, sound argument.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: On the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ (3) is a magnification of it. يَوْمَ is accusative by "will come" (ستأتي), on the view of whoever implied it; and whoever did not imply it, the implied form according to him is: "the Calamity (will be on the day…)" [Translator's note: i.e., يوم is governed by القارعة].

nahhas-irab:4-5.t: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَراشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ (4): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of يكون; and likewise وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ (5). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd): (كالصوف) "like wool". And al-ʿihn is the plural of ʿihna.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ said: موازينه, i.e., his weight.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: Mujāhid said: he is pleased with it. Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied form in Arabic is "possessing pleasure", by way of relation (nasab).

nahhas-irab:8-9.t:
The view of al-Akhfash is that the meaning of أمّه is "his resting place", and هاوية is a fire; and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 583-
هوت أمّه ما يبعث الصّبح غاديا ... وماذا يؤدّي اللّيل حين يؤوب
(May his mother perish! What does the morning send forth when he sets out early, and what does the night bring back when he returns?)
Others said: «فأمّه هاوية»: its original is هاوٍ, i.e., perishing, because the umm of a thing is its origin and its bulk; from this, al-Ḥamd (al-Fātiḥa) was called the "Mother of the Qur'an", and from it is the saying of the poet: [al-Wāfir] 584-
لأمّ الأرض ويل ما أجنّت ... غداة أضرّ بالحسن السّبيل
(Woe to the mother of the earth, for what it has concealed, on the morning when the road came near to al-Ḥasan.)

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), in all three places; the khabar (predicate) of the first and the third is (القارعة), and the khabar of the second is the clause أدراك; (the wāw) before it is parenthetical. (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "تقرع" [Note: or "تأتي"; or it is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر".], (كالفراش) is attached to the khabar of يكون [Note: or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الناس if the verb (يكون) is a complete verb, i.e. they exist in the place of assembly in the state of being like moths], and likewise (كالعهن)..
Clause: «القارعة ما القارعة ... » has no grammatical position; it is an inceptive clause.
And the clause: «ما القارعة ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (القارعة).
And the clause: «ما أدراك ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause: «أدراك ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «ما القارعة ... » is in the position of accusative, the second direct object of the verb أدراك.
And the clause: « (تقرع) يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «يكون الناس ... » is in the position of genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تكون الجبال ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يكون الناس.

* Morphology:
(4) الفراش: a collective noun (ism jamʿ); its singular is فراشة; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(5) المنفوش: a passive participle from the triliteral نفش; its wazn is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Tashbīh mursal mujmal (simile with the particle of comparison stated and the point of likeness omitted): in His saying, the Exalted: «يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَراشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ».
A magnificent simile: they are likened to scattered, flying moths in their multitude and dispersal, weakness and abasement, coming and going without order, and flying toward the caller from every direction when he calls them to the place of assembly.
Tashbīh mursal mujmal: in His saying, the Exalted: «وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ».
Here the mountains are likened to carded wool dyed in various colours, in the scattering of their parts and their flying about in the air, as His saying, the Exalted, declares: «وَتَرَى الْجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ».

safi-cedvel:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(the fāʾ) is resumptive. (أمّا) is a particle of condition and elaboration. (من) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (the fāʾ) is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis of أمّا. (في عيشة) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is هو..
Clause: «من ثقلت موازينه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ثقلت موازينه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «هو في عيشة ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
8-11 (the wāw) is a conjunction. (أمّا من ... هاوية) is like أمّا من ... في عيشة. (the wāw) is parenthetical. (ما أدراك ما هيه) is like ما أدراك ما القارعة [Note: in verse (3) of this sūra.], and (the hāʾ) in (هيه) is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt), with no grammatical position. (نار) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي".
And the clause: «من خفّت موازينه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من ثقلت ...
And the clause: «خفّت موازينه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «أمّه هاوية ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «ما أدراك ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause: «أدراك ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «ما هيه» is in the position of accusative, the second direct object of the verb أدراك.
And the clause: « (هي) نار ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(9) هاوية: the feminine of الهاوي, an active participle from هوى يهوي (class of ضرب); its wazn is فاعل; or it is a proper name for the Fire, on the wazn فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymy): in His saying, the Exalted: «فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ».
The relation of this majāz is locality, because the one who is pleased with it is the one who lives in it. It was also said: راضية means مرضية (pleasing).
2- Simile: in His saying, the Exalted: «فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ».
Here the place of refuge is expressed as "mother" by way of likening it to her, for the mother is the child's refuge and shelter; and in it is mockery of him. It was also said that the Fire is likened to a mother in that it encompasses him as the mother's womb encompasses her child.

* Benefits:
- The hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt):
It is the hāʾ that is attached to show a vowel or a letter, as in His saying, the Exalted (وَما أَدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ), and our saying (هاهناه) (وا زيداه). Its origin is that one stops on it. Sometimes it is joined in connected speech with the intention of stopping. The hāʾ of pause occurs in His saying, the Exalted (ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ. هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ).

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {القارعة مَا القارعة}: like His saying {الحاقة مَا الحآقة} [al-Ḥāqqa: 12] and like His saying {وَأَصْحَابُ اليمين مَآ أَصْحَابُ اليمين} [al-Wāqiʿa: 27]; both have been treated earlier. You have already learned from what Makkī transmitted that it is permissible to put «القارعة» in the nominative by an implied verb that governs «يومَ» in the accusative. It was also said that the meaning of the sentence is one of warning (taḥdhīr). Al-Zajjāj said: "The Arabs warn and urge (tughrī) with the nominative as with the accusative." And he recited:
4631 - لَجَديرون بالوفاءِ إذا ق ... لَ أخو النجدةِ السِّلاحُ السِّلاحُ
(They are indeed fit for loyalty when the man of valour says: "Arms! Arms!")
I say: this was already treated in His saying {نَاقَةَ الله} [al-Shams: 13], for the one who read it in the nominative. And what shows this is the reading of ʿĪsā, {القارعةَ ما القارعةَ} in the accusative, by an implied verb, that is, "beware of the Striking Calamity", with «ما» redundant (zāʾida). The second «القارعة» is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī).

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَكُونُ}: there are several views on what governs it. The first: an implied verb which «القارعةُ» indicates, that is, "it strikes them on the day when it comes"; it was also said that the implied form is "the Striking Calamity comes on the day". The second: that it is an implied «اذْكُرْ» ("remember"), so that it is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) and not an adverbial (ẓarf). The third: that it is «القارعة»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī said so. Al-Shaykh said: "If Ibn ʿAṭiyya meant the first word, that is not permissible, because of the separation between the governor, which is within the ṣila (relative clause) of the definite article al-, and the governed word by a foreign element, namely the khabar. And if he made «القارعة» a proper name for the Resurrection, it does not govern either. And if he meant the second and the third, the meaning of adverbial time does not fit with it." The fourth: that it is an implied verb that puts the first «القارعةُ» in the nominative, as if it had been said: "the Striking Calamity comes on the day when it happens"; Makkī said so. On this, what lies between would be a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ), which is very far-fetched and out of tune with the construction of the sentence. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يومُ» in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "its time is the day when it happens".
His saying: {كالفراش}: it may be the khabar of the incomplete verb (kāna al-nāqiṣa), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of the complete verb (kāna al-tāmma), that is, "they will be found and gathered in the likeness of moths (al-farāsh)". It is a well-known flying creature. It was also said: it is the gnats (al-hamaj) among mosquitoes, locusts and the like; the proverb of giddiness and recklessness is struck with it. One says: "lighter-witted than a moth", and the following was recited:
4632 - فَراشَةُ الحُلْمِ فِرْعَوْنُ العذابِ وإنْ ... يُطْلَبُ نَداه فكَلْبٌ دونَه كَلْبُ
(A moth in forbearance, a Pharaoh in punishment; and if his generosity is sought, a dog, and a dog behind him.)
And another said:
4633 - وقد كانَ أقوامٌ رَدَدْتُ قلوبَهُمْ ... عليهم وكانوا كالفَراشِ من الجهلِ
(There were people whose hearts I restored to them, and they were like moths in ignorance.)
Al-farāsha is also the little water in a vessel, and "the farāsha of the lock" is so called from its resemblance to the moth. In likening people to moths there are various kinds of emphasis (mubālagha), among them: the giddiness that afflicts them, their spreading over the earth, their mounting one another, their great number, weakness and abasement, their coming without going away, their heading for the caller from every direction, and their flying toward the fire. Jarīr said:
4634 - إنَّ الفرزدقَ ما عَلِمْتَ وقومَه ... مثلُ الفَراشِ غَشِيْنَ نارَ المُصْطَلي
(Al-Farazdaq, as you know, and his people are like moths that have flocked to the fire of the one warming himself.)
And al-ʿihn was treated under Saʾala.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ}: that is, perishing (hālika). This is a proverb. They say of one who perishes: "his mother has fallen" (hawat ummuhu), because when he perishes his mother falls in bereavement and grief. On this is the saying of the poet:
463 - 5- هَوَتْ أمُّه ما يَبْعَثُ الصبحُ غادياً ... وماذا يَرُدُّ الليلُ حين يَؤُوْبُ
(His mother is bereaved! What does the morning send forth as it goes out, and what does the night bring back when it returns!)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed in the source as «463 - 5-», evidently 4635, following 4634 in the preceding entry.]
Ṭalḥa read «فإمُّه» with kasra on the hamza. Ibn Khālawayh transmitted from Ibn Durayd that it is a dialect form. The grammarians do not allow this except when a kasra or a yāʾ precedes it. The verification of this was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, together with the disagreement of the readers on it.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {مَا هِيَهْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar standing in the place of the two objects of «أَدْراك»; this is a case of suspension (taʿlīq). «هي» is a pronoun referring to al-hāwiya, if al-hāwiya is, as has been said, a name for one of the levels (darakāt) of the Fire; otherwise it refers to the calamity (al-dāhiya) understood from al-hāwiya. Ḥamza dropped the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakta) in running speech. The verification of this was given in al-Ḥāqqa. «نارٌ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "it is a fire".

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْقَارِعَةُ (١) مَا الْقَارِعَةُ (٢)).
The discussion of its beginning is like the discussion of the beginning of al-Ḥāqqa.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ يَكُونُ): its governor (ʿāmil) is «الْقَارِعَةُ», or what it indicates.
It is also said that the implied form is: «اذْكُرُوا» (remember).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ (٧)).
(رَاضِيَةٍ) has been discussed in al-Ḥāqqa.

ukberi-tibyan:9-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ (٩) وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ (١٠) نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ (١١)).
The hāʾ in «هِيَهْ» is the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt); whoever retains it in continuous recitation treats it as in pause, so that the verse endings do not differ. (نَارٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هِيَ نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ» (it is a blazing fire).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qāriʿa
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿القارِعَةُ﴾ ﴿ما القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 2] ("the Striking Calamity; what is the Striking Calamity?"): ”اَلْقارِعَةُ“, ”اَلْواقِعَةُ“ and ”اَلْحاقَّةُ“ are among the attributes of the Hour of Resurrection. ”اَلْقارِعَةُ“ is the one that strikes with terrors. We have already explained the iʿrāb of ﴿الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 1] ﴿ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 2], and like it is ﴿القارِعَةُ﴾ ﴿ما القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 2].

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النّاسُ كالفَراشِ المَبْثُوثِ﴾ ("the Day when people will be like scattered moths"): ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb (ẓarf); the meaning is: "it will be on the Day when people are like scattered moths". ”اَلْفَراشُ“ is what you see like small gnats, falling headlong into a fire. He likened people at the time of the Resurrection to spreading locusts and to scattered moths, because when they are resurrected they surge into one another, like locusts that surge into one another.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿كالعِهْنِ المَنفُوشِ﴾ ("like carded wool"): ”اَلْعِهْنُ“ is wool; its unit noun is ”عِهْنَةٌ“. One says ”عِهْنَةٌ“ and ”عِهْنٌ“, like ”صُوفَةٌ“ and ”صُوفٌ“.

zajjaj:6-7.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأمّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾ ﴿فَهُوَ في عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ﴾ ("as for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life"): [rāḍiya means] possessed of pleasure. Its meaning is: whose scales are heavy with good deeds, as you say ”لِفُلانٍ عِنْدِي وزْنٌ ثَقِيلٌ“ ("so-and-so has heavy weight with me"), whose interpretation is: he has heavy weight in good. And the meaning of ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ﴾ is: possessed of pleasure, with which whoever lives in it is pleased. Some said its meaning is "pleasing (marḍiyya)", and that comes back to this same meaning in the exegesis.

zajjaj:8-9.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأمّا مَن خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾ ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ﴾ ("but as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss"): that is, his dwelling is the Fire. His dwelling was called "his mother" because the root [of finding rest] is in taking refuge with mothers, so [the word] was substituted for what he takes refuge in: ﴿نارٌ حامِيَةٌ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 11] ("a blazing Fire").

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ ("and what will make you know what it is?"): the pausal form is ”هِيَهْ“, and the connected form is ”هِيَ نارٌ حامِيَةٌ“; but the hāʾ entered in pause to make clear the fatḥa of the yāʾ. What is obligatory is to follow the Muṣḥaf: one pauses on it and does not connect, and reads: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ ﴿نارٌ حامِيَةٌ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 11], because the Sunna is to follow the Muṣḥaf, and the hāʾ is written in it.
